title: Planetary friendships in Vedic astrology, and why they aren't mutual | Ask Tota
description: The Moon counts Mercury a friend. Mercury counts the Moon an enemy. Here is the full naisargika table, the temporal overlay, and the five-fold combination.
og_title: The Moon likes Mercury. Mercury does not like the Moon.
og_description: Planetary friendship is not mutual, and there are two separate systems that combine into five levels. Here is the whole thing.
dek: the moon counts mercury as a friend. mercury counts the moon as an enemy. that asymmetry is real, it is in the classical tables, and it is one of two friendship systems that combine into five levels. here is all of it.

faq.q: what is planetary friendship in vedic astrology?
faq.a: a classification of how comfortable each graha is in another's sign. naisargika maitri is the permanent version, fixed for every chart, and it decides how well a graha functions when it sits in territory somebody else owns.
often, but not always. the moon counts mercury as a friend while mercury counts the moon as an enemy. the tables are derived separately for each graha, so asymmetry is built in.
from each graha's mooltrikona sign. grahas whose signs fall in the 2nd, 4th, 5th, 8th, 9th and 12th from it are friends, the rest are enemies, and those that qualify both ways come out neutral.

tatkalika maitri, which depends on the chart. grahas in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th or 12th house from each other are temporary friends. those in the 1st, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th or 9th are temporary enemies.
the five-fold friendship, made by combining the natural and temporal tables. the five levels are adhimitra, mitra, sama, shatru and adhishatru: great friend, friend, neutral, enemy, great enemy.
because a graha in a friend's sign functions comfortably and one in an enemy's sign does not. it sits in the middle of the dignity ladder, between own sign and debilitation.

faq.q: does the moon have any enemies?
faq.a: no. in the standard naisargika table the moon counts the sun and mercury as friends and everything else as neutral. it is the only graha with no natural enemy.
mercury and venus. it counts the sun, moon and mars as enemies and jupiter as neutral. that pattern lines up neatly with saturn being a yogakaraka for the two venus-ruled ascendants.
the lord of the sign a graha sits in. checking whether a graha is a friend of its own dispositor is one of the quickest useful reads in a chart.

faq.q: where does friendship sit in the dignity ladder?
faq.a: the usual ordering, strongest first, is exalted, mooltrikona, own sign, great friend's sign, friend's sign, neutral, enemy's sign, great enemy's sign, debilitated.

faq.q: do the friendship tables apply to rahu and ketu?
faq.a: not in the standard naisargika table, because the nodes own no signs. practitioners generally read them through their dispositor and their companions instead.

faq.q: do all texts give the same friendship table?
faq.a: the naisargika table is broadly consistent across sources, with minor variation. the derivation from mooltrikona is what makes it stable, since it follows from sign positions rather than opinion.
